user_query: Under what condition does LINE(1st+2nd) perform significantly better than all other methods, and what does this suggest about the two proximities in LINE?
llm_response: LINE(1st+2nd) performs significantly better when the graph contains both strong local pairwise connections and broader neighborhood/structural similarity signals, so that first-order and second-order proximities are both informative and complementary. This suggests that the two proximities in LINE capture different aspects of network structure and that combining them yields a more complete embedding than using either one alone.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is a high-level interpretation consistent with LINE’s design and reported comparative behavior, but the exact experimental condition depends on the specific benchmark or dataset referenced.
